content: 1. Thirumurthy H, Masters SH, Rao S, Bronson MA, Lanham M, Omanga E, et al. conducted a randomized clinical trial in Kenya to evaluate the impact of conditional economic compensation on the uptake of voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC). The study was published in JAMA in 2014, volume 312, pages 703-711. 2. Thornton R and Godlonton S explored how pricing influences the risk profile of individuals opting for medical male circumcision. Their findings were published in Preventive Medicine in 2016, volume 92, pages 68-73. 3. Wilson N, Frade S, Rech D, and Friedman W examined the role of advertising in creating demand for voluntary medical male circumcision. Their study appeared in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016, volume 72, Supplement 4, pages S288-S291. 4. Zanolini A, Bolton C, Lyabola LL, Phiri G, Samona A, Kaonga A, et al. assessed the feasibility and effectiveness of a peer referral incentive intervention to promote male circumcision uptake in Zambia. This research was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016, volume 72, Supplement 4, pages S257-S263. 5. Semeere AS, Castelnuovo B, Bbaale DS, Kiragga AN, Kigozi J, Muganzi AM, et al. piloted an innovative demand creation strategy for VMMC targeting high-impact male populations by engaging pregnant women at antenatal clinics in Kampala, Uganda. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016, volume 72, Supplement 4, pages S273-S279. 6. Bazant E, Mahler H, Machaku M, Lemwayi R, Kulindwa Y, Gisenge Lija J, et al. conducted a randomized evaluation of a demand creation lottery for VMMC among adults in Tanzania. The study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016, volume 72, Supplement 4, pages S280-S287. 7. The World Health Organization (WHO) released a progress brief on VMMC for HIV prevention in 14 priority countries in East and Southern Africa. This document was accessed on June 22, 2020. 8. UNAIDS published data in 2017 through the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS, providing insights into global HIV trends and interventions. The report was accessed on May 30, 2019. 9. Evens E, Lanham M, Murray K, Rao S, Agot K, Omanga E, et al. conducted qualitative interviews with male participants and their partners in a randomized controlled trial to understand the use of economic compensation to increase demand for VMMC in Kenya. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016, volume 72, Supplement 4, pages S306-S310. 10. Fisher JA discussed the concept of voluntariness in informed consent, emphasizing structural coercion and the influence of social and economic contexts. This analysis was published in the Kennedy Institute of Ethics Journal in 2013, volume 23, pages 355-379. 11. Lunze K and Paasche-Orlow MK examined the ethical safeguards required when using financial incentives to promote healthy behavior, particularly in the context of behavioral economics. Their work appeared in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine in 2013, volume 44, pages 659-665. 12. Wirth KE, Semo BW, Spees LP, Ntsuape C, Barnhart S, Ledikwe JH, et al. conducted a prospective cohort study in Botswana to evaluate the safety and patient satisfaction associated with VMMC. The study was published in PLoS One in 2017, volume 12, article e0185904. 13. Blumenthal-Barby JS and Burroughs H explored the ethical implications of using behavioral nudges to improve healthcare outcomes. Their work was published in the American Journal of Bioethics in 2012, volume 12, pages 1-10. 14. The United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) released a report in 2009 addressing the promotion and protection of human rights, including the right to development, with a focus on extreme poverty. The report was accessed on June 6, 2019. 15. Pascoe L and Peacock D analyzed national policies in Eastern and Southern Africa to address the health needs of men and boys. Their findings were published by Sonke Gender Justice in 2017 and accessed on June 12, 2019. 16. WHO published a framework for implementing VMMC for HIV prevention from 2017 to 2021, with a meeting report dated February 27 to March 1, 2017. The document was accessed on June 7, 2019. 17. WHO released guidelines on digital interventions for health system strengthening, providing evidence-based recommendations. The document was accessed on June 7, 2019. 18. A promising practice report highlighted Zambia's SMS pilot program for VMMC demand creation among adolescents and young adults. The report was accessed on February 26, 2020. 19. Shaba F, Menego G, Kapito M, Gibson H, Davis S, Flowers N, et al. presented findings on using sexually transmitted infection clinics as platforms to reach high-risk men for VMMC in Malawi. This was shared at the International Conference on AIDS and STIs in Africa (ICASA) in December 2019. 20. Downs JA, Mwakisole AH, Chandika AB, Lugoba S, Kassim R, Laizer E, et al. conducted a cluster randomized trial in Tanzania to educate religious leaders on promoting male circumcision uptake. The study was published in The Lancet in 2017, volume 389, pages 1124-1132. 21. Mwandii Z, Zita F, Tanque M, Sarama D, Devos P, Gaspar, et al. shared achievements and lessons learned in optimizing site capacity for VMMC programs in Mozambique. This was presented at the 22nd International AIDS Conference in July 2018. 22. Dickson KE, Tran NT, Samuelson JL, Njeuhmeli E, Cherutich P, Dick B, et al. analyzed policy and program implementation frameworks for VMMC in Eastern and Southern Africa. Their findings were published in PLoS Medicine in 2011, volume 8. 23. The Zimbabwe Smart-LyncAges Project focused on sustaining VMMC services and linking them with adolescent sexual and reproductive health. The report was accessed on February 26, 2020. 24. Makawa D highlighted efforts in Zambia to collaborate with traditional leaders to promote male circumcision. The report was accessed on February 26, 2020. 25. PEPFAR released a service guide for best practices in VMMC site operations. The document was accessed on July 5, 2020. 26. Wambura M, Mahler H, Grund JM, Larke N, Mshana G, Kuringe E, et al. investigated strategies to increase VMMC uptake among adult men in Tanzania. Their study was published in AIDS in 2017, volume 31, pages 1025-1034. 27. WHO's framework for strengthening health systems to improve outcomes was accessed on July 12, 2019. 28. The World Health Report 2000 focused on improving health system performance. The report was accessed on June 10, 2020. 29. WHO published a handbook on monitoring health system building blocks, including indicators and measurement strategies. The document was accessed on July 12, 2019. 30. WHO released a report on sustainable health financing, universal coverage, and social health insurance. The document was accessed on July 12, 2019. 31. Ledikwe JH, Nyanga RO, Hagon J, Grignon JS, Mpofu M, Semo BW, et al. reviewed lessons learned from scaling up VMMC programs. Their findings were published in HIV/AIDS (Auckland, NZ) in 2014, volume 6, page 139. 32. Mathauer I, Dale E, Meessen B summarized key policy issues and questions related to strategic purchasing for universal health coverage. The document was accessed on July 16, 2019. 33. Luo C, Kaliel D, Njeuhmeli E, Benson FN, Gorgens M, Christensen A, et al. discussed strategies for scaling up and sustaining VMMC to maintain HIV prevention benefits. Their work was published in Global Health Science and Practice in 2016, volume 4, pages S9-S17. 34. Perry L, Rech D, Mavhu W, Frade S, Machaku MD, Onyango M, et al. examined work experience, job fulfillment, and burnout among VMMC providers in Kenya, South Africa, Tanzania, and Zimbabwe. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2014, volume 9, article e84215. 35. WHO's framework on integrated, people-centered health services was accessed on July 12, 2019. 36. A systematic review by WHO examined the global experience of community health workers in delivering health-related Millennium Development Goals. The report was accessed on July 12, 2019. 37. WHO published models and tools for health workforce planning and projections. The document was accessed on July 12, 2019. 38. WHO released a joint strategic action framework to accelerate the scale-up of VMMC for HIV prevention in Eastern and Southern Africa. The document was accessed on July 12, 2019. 39. Bulled N and Green EC discussed engaging the traditional sector to make VMMC a viable HIV prevention strategy in high-prevalence countries. Their work was published in Critical Public Health in 2016, volume 26, pages 258-268. 40. WHO's Health Workforce 2030 strategy aimed at developing a global approach to human resources for health. The document was accessed on July 12, 2019. 41. Edgil D, Stankard P, Forsythe S, Rech D, Chrouser K, Adamu T, et al. outlined logistics, commodities, and waste management requirements for scaling up VMMC services. Their study was published in PLoS Medicine in 2011, volume 8, article e1001128. 42. WHO emphasized strengthening surgical care systems by developing national surgical, obstetric, and anesthesia plans. The document was accessed on July 12, 2019. 43. Storr J, Twyman A, Zingg W, Damani N, Kilpatrick C, Reilly J, et al. identified core components for effective infection prevention and control programs based on new WHO recommendations. Their findings were published in Antimicrobial Resistance and Infection Control in 2017, volume 6, article 6. 44. WHO's global health sector strategy on HIV for 2016-2021 was accessed on July 12, 2019. 45. Koller TS, Saint V, Floranita R, Koemara Sakti GM, Pambudi I, Hermawan L, et al. applied the Innov8 approach to review national health programs in Indonesia, ensuring inclusivity. Their findings were published in Global Health Action in 2018, volume 11, pages 63-69. 46. WHO's framework on integrated, people-centered health services was accessed on July 12, 2019. 47. WHO published a process for making strategic choices in health systems to improve the quality of care. The document was accessed on June 9, 2020. 48. The VMMC CQI and EQA Toolkit provided resources for demand creation in VMMC programs. The toolkit was accessed on July 15, 2019. 49. Kripke K, Njeuhmeli E, Samuelson J, Schnure M, Dalal S, Farley T, et al. assessed progress, impact, and next steps in rolling out VMMC for HIV prevention in 14 priority countries in Eastern and Southern Africa through 2014. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2016, volume 11, article e0158767. 50. The AIDS Law Brief addressed the age of consent for HIV testing, counseling, and treatment in Tanzania. The document was accessed on July 12, 2019. 51. Sgaier SK, Reed JB, Thomas A, Njeuhmeli E discussed lessons and challenges in managing VMMC programs to achieve HIV prevention impact. Their work was published in PLoS Medicine in 2014, volume 11, article e1001641. 52. WHO's community engagement framework for quality, people-centered, and resilient health services was accessed on July 12, 2019.
